title: Repeated Billing Error Uplift on Fixed-Price Line Carrying Credits
content:
> Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts: fixed-price line corrections: repeated billing error.

The fixed-price line carrying rate is raised for a repeated billing error on the contract: 2 or more rebill credits for cycles other than the pass-through cycle posted on the contract in the twelve months before the handling date multiply it by 1.50, one such credit multiplies it by 1.25, and none leaves it unchanged.

The credits counted are the contract's rebill credit lines posted in the window whose cycle is not the pass-through cycle, a rebill credit being dated to the cycle of the line it corrects. A line falls in the twelve months before the handling date when it was posted on or before the handling date and fewer than twelve whole calendar months have passed from its posted date to the handling date, a month being complete on the same day of the month as the posted date.

| Rebill credits for other cycles in the twelve months | Carrying rate multiplied by |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 1.50 |
| 1 | 1.25 |
| none | 1, unchanged |

## Cases (hypothetical)

- Carrying rate 0.03 and two earlier credits for other cycles in the twelve months: 0.03 multiplied by 1.50, that is 0.045.
- Carrying rate 0.06 and one such credit: 0.075.
- A rebill credit already on the pass-through cycle itself is not counted.
